subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers close, adopt, or replace the open conflicting fork PR before allowing a narrow active-runtime fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is narrow and source-proven, but the issue has an open closing PR in a fork plus `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr` and `clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review` state, so automation should not queue another fix until maintainers decide the fate of that candidate.

options.title: Close and replace the fork candidate
options.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork PR, then allow a narrow fix against `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts` with live Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt the fork branch
options.body: Have a maintainer retarget the fork work to the active runtime path, remove unrelated docs churn, and gather real Telegram proof.

options.title: Keep waiting on the fork
options.body: Leave the fork PR open, accepting that current main remains broken and ClawSweeper should not queue a duplicate fix yet.

recommendation.title: Close and replace the fork candidate
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the conflicting fork PR, then allow a narrow fix against `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts` with live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the native approval lifecycle refactor that owns the active runtime seam involved in the clean fix.
